content:
A gunman is dead after he opened fire inside a gym in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood on Thursday morning, killing one person and wounding four others, including one who remains in critical condition.

The suspect barricaded himself in a nearby apartment in the same building after the shooting, where officers later found him dead with a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

“We do believe that the suspect is now contained in that location,” interim Metropolitan Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said at a news conference, adding that the scene remained “fluid.”

While police had not identified the gunman as of Thursday afternoon, multiple publications identified the suspect as 55-year-old medical doctor Matt Lambert.

Carrol said investigators believe the shooting stemmed from a dispute between Lambert and the residential building’s homeowners association.

Lambert had filed a lawsuit alleging that the building’s condo association failed to act on his complaints about a mold problem and water damage inside his unit, The Washington Post reported.

The deceased victim was the building’s property manager, Ward 2 D.C. Council member Brooke Pinto said.

Officers arrived within 30 seconds of the first call, which came in just before 8 a.m., Carroll said. Police negotiators spoke with the suspect for more than an hour before officers heard a gunshot inside the seventh-floor apartment and forced their way in.

Sebastian Murdock contributed to this report.
